newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Hepworth targets East Europe, China.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Hepworth targets East Europe, China.

text.p: UK heating and building materials group Hepworth Plc said on Friday its sights are set firmly on further expansion in eastern Europe and China as it seeks growth through new markets and new products.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive John Carter said Hepworth is in advanced talks about a number of projects in China, where it is already building two factories to make gas boilers and mains water pipes.
"We are at the detailed planning stages on a number of initiatives and that it all I can say," Carter said following the publication of better than expected interim results.

Although Hepworth reported a drop in first-half pre-tax profit to 35.5 million stg from 37.5 million stg a year before, the results beat analysts' forecasts and bucked the sharply weaker trend seen in the rest of the building materials sector.

"Markets have been quite tough," Carter said, attributing Hepworth's relatively "robust" performance to the impact of efficiency gains and a focus on international markets. "We have improved to the point where we can export internationally, and that is going on across all parts of the group," he said.
The UK operations exported more than a quarter of their output, with first-half exports up 24 percent to 66 million stg.

Hepworth is particularly keen to expand its pipes business in China, with its system of flexible, plastic plumbing products high on the list. "The infrastructure demand in China continues developing at a very strong pace and we want to introduce all our new, innovative technology in China," he said.

Hepworth is also interested in moving into other parts of south-east Asia. In eastern Europe, Carter said the group plans to expand from its base in Poland into neighboring countries in the next six to 12 months, through greenfield projects, joint ventures and acquisitions.
"Heating is our spearhead project," he said.

Hepworth's other strategic move is the expansion of its air conditioning operations in France, Spain and Italy, where Carter said it can build on its existing strength in gas boilers. The group is building an air-conditioning plant in Spain.
Carter said the group's low gearing, which fell to 15.6 percent in the first half from 22.3 percent a year before, "does give us the opportunity to fulfil more of our ambitions."

Carter said the group will continue to review its dividend policy regularly. Hepworth left its interim payout unchanged at 5.5 pence. "We consider the level of the dividend we paid to be appropriate for the group in its current position," he added.
